title: Quasi-coherent cohomology of the naive cotangent complex of an arbitrary space morphism
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $h:X\to Y$ any morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], with the size conventions [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathrm{NL}_{X/Y}$ be the two-term naive cotangent complex on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ of [def-sfb-space-naive-cotangent-complex], regarded in $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Its cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and vanish outside degrees $-1,0$. In particular $\mathrm{NL}_{X/Y}$ belongs to $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$, the full subcategory with quasi-coherent cohomology. No finite-presentation, Noetherian, quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness assumption is imposed on $h$, $X$ or $Y$.

proof.text: Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $V\to Y$. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], $Z=X\times_YV$ is an algebraic space and $Z\to X$ is surjective etale. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $W\to Z$, using [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Thus $W\to X$ is surjective etale: after base change to any scheme over $X$, both maps are scheme etale covers, whose composite is an etale cover by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-composition]. Cover $W$ by affine opens $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ each mapping into an affine open $V_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i$ of $V$: inverse images of an affine-open cover of $V$ are open, and each has an affine-open cover. Open inclusions are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. Testing on schemes and composing covers as above shows that the maps $p_i:U_i\to X$ are jointly surjective etale and that $q_i:V_i\to Y$ are etale. The maps $g_i:U_i\to V_i$ satisfy $hp_i=q_ig_i$. No finite subcover and no affineness of intersections is used.

proof.text: For each of these squares, [lem-sfb-space-naive-cotangent-etale-localization] gives $\mathrm{NL}_{X/Y}|_{U_i}\simeq\mathrm{NL}_{U_i/V_i}$. Choose the polynomial presentation $P_i=R_i[x_b\mid b\in B_i]\twoheadrightarrow B_i$, $x_b\mapsto b$, which is surjective because every $b$ is the image of $x_b$, and put $I_i=\ker(P_i\to B_i)$. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-etale-naive-cotangent-presentation] with this possibly infinite set of variables: in $D(\mathcal O_{U_i})$ the restricted complex is isomorphic to $[A_i\xrightarrow{d_i}E_i]$ in degrees $-1,0$, where $A_i=(I_i/I_i^2)^{\sim}_{\mathrm{et}}$ and $E_i=(B_i\otimes_{P_i}\Omega_{P_i/R_i})^{\sim}_{\mathrm{et}}$. Each underlying module has a quasi-coherent associated Zariski sheaf by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]; [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] says its associated small-etale sheaf is quasi-coherent. Thus both $A_i$ and $E_i$ are quasi-coherent without any finite-generation assertion.

proof.text: For the two-term model of step 2 the cohomology sheaves are $\ker(d_i)$ in degree $-1$, $\operatorname{coker}(d_i)$ in degree $0$, and zero in all other degrees. Both kernel and cokernel, taken in all module sheaves, are quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits], applied to the scheme $U_i$ regarded as an algebraic space. Restriction to $U_i$ is the exact functor of [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. Consequently it preserves kernels, images and cokernels, so $H^n(\mathrm{NL}_{X/Y})|_{U_i}=H^n(\mathrm{NL}_{X/Y}|_{U_i})$. The derived isomorphisms of step 2 identify these with the cohomology sheaves just computed. This uses an exact localization, not tensor pullback along an arbitrary morphism.

source.place: Tag 0D0Y, lemma-netherlander-quasi-coherent; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03M1 (lemma-properties-quasi-coherent), clause (3); exact localization as in sites-modules.tex Tag 03DJ.

proof.text: Fix $n\in\{-1,0\}$ and write $F=H^n(\mathrm{NL}_{X/Y})$. We verify directly the local-presentation definition [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. On each $U_i$, step 3 says $F|_{U_i}$ is quasi-coherent; choose an etale covering $U_{ia}\to U_i$ on which it has a free presentation $\mathcal O^{(J_{ia})}\to\mathcal O^{(K_{ia})}\to F\to0$. For any object $T\to X$ of $X_{\mathrm{et}}$, base change gives a covering by schemes $T\times_XU_i\to T$ by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]; further base change by $U_{ia}\to U_i$ and composition gives an etale cover $T\times_XU_{ia}\to T$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-composition]. Restrict the displayed presentations to these slice sites. Restriction is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], and a free sheaf restricts to the free sheaf on the same index set: its local sections are locally finite sums of the same basis symbols with coefficients in the restricted structure sheaf. Hence the restricted sequences are the required local free presentations of $F|_T$. Since $T$ was arbitrary, $F$ is quasi-coherent. The zero sheaf has the empty presentation and is also quasi-coherent.

source.place: Tag 03M0, lemma-characterize-quasi-coherent, local-presentation argument for (3) implies (1), written for a covering family.

proof.text: By [def-sfb-space-naive-cotangent-complex] the original complex itself has zero terms outside degrees $-1,0$. In every other degree both its cycles and boundaries are zero, so its cohomology vanishes. Step 4 gives quasi-coherence in the two remaining degrees and for the zero sheaves. Thus every cohomology sheaf is quasi-coherent, which is precisely membership in the full subcategory $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ specified in the statement. All constructions allowed arbitrary small generating sets and arbitrary etale covers; none required finiteness, Noetherianness or separation.
